title: Interoperable Digital Building Twins Through Communicating Materials and Semantic BIM
justification: IC1 is satisfied: the abstract is explicitly about “Digital Building Twins (DBT)” and provides an explicit understanding/definition of a DBT as a “lively representation of a buildings' status and environment,” indicating the digital twin is central. IC2 is only weakly/ambiguously satisfied: it claims Semantic Web technologies enable “explainable decision-support,” but does not explicitly describe any concrete explainability/XAI mechanism (method, model, interface, evaluation, or formal analysis) within the digital twin beyond this label. IC3 is not satisfied: the abstract does not explicitly define any human roles (operator/decision-maker/analyst) nor describe human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop or human-centered interaction in the system architecture or evaluation. Since all criteria must be explicitly met and IC3 is missing (and IC2 lacks concrete mechanism detail), the article is excluded.

title: Developing DELPHI expert consensus rules for a digital twin model of acute stroke care in the neuro critical care unit
justification:
IC1 (Digital Twin central): Satisfied. The paper’s purpose is to develop DELPHI consensus rules specifically “for the development of a digital twin model for use in the neurologic ICU,” and the rules are intended to “inform the construction of the digital twin model.”

IC2 (Explicit XAI/interpretability within DT context): Satisfied. The conclusion explicitly makes an interpretability claim tied to the digital-twin approach: “digital twin AI created by the DELPHI process are easily interpretable models” compared to associative AI.

IC3 (Explicit human roles or human-in/on-the-loop interaction in system/evaluation): Not satisfied. The only human involvement described is an expert panel participating in DELPHI during rule elicitation/model development. The abstract does not explicitly define any runtime human role (e.g., clinician/operator/decision-maker) in the digital twin’s use, nor any human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop mechanism or human-centered interaction as part of the system architecture or evaluation. Because IC3 is missing, the article must be excluded under Phase 3 rules.

title: Visual analytics for digital twins: a conceptual framework and case study
justification: IC1 is satisfied: the work is explicitly centered on “visual analytics for digital twins,” proposing a “conceptual visual analytics framework for digital twins (DTVA)” and analyzing DT visual representation, analytical reasoning, and a human–machine interface within the DT context. IC3 is satisfied: the abstract explicitly positions humans as decision-makers/analysts (“navigating humans through twin data,” integrating “human domain experience and cognitive abilities”) and includes a “human–machine interface (DTI)” component as part of the framework. IC2 is NOT satisfied: the abstract does not explicitly propose, implement, evaluate, or formally analyze explainability/interpretability/transparency/XAI mechanisms in the digital twin context; it focuses on visual analytics, guidance, and decision support without unambiguous XAI language or clearly described explainability methods. Per Phase 3 rules, missing IC2 requires exclusion.

title: A DT framework integrating human and artificial intelligence for power consumption prediction in CNC machining
justification: IC1 satisfied: The paper centrally proposes and applies a “human-centric digital twin framework (HCDT)” / “applied digital twin (ADT)” for a specific CNC milling machine, aligned with ISO 23247, and the DT is the core system concept. IC2 not satisfied: Although the abstract states “the addition of explainability… has developed the trustworthiness,” it does not explicitly describe any explainability/XAI mechanism (e.g., feature attributions, rule extraction, interpretable model choice justified as explainable, explanation interface, transparency metrics) being proposed, implemented, or evaluated within the DT; the mention is vague and non-specific. IC3 not satisfied: The abstract claims the DT “incorporates human intelligence” and is “human-centric,” but it does not explicitly define human roles (operator/engineer/decision-maker) nor describe a concrete human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop interaction, workflow, or evaluation involving humans. Because IC2 and IC3 are ambiguous/unsupported by explicit abstract evidence, the article must be excluded under Phase 3 rules.

title: Urban Digital Twins and metaverses towards city multiplicities: uniting or dividing urban experiences?
justification: IC1 is satisfied: the article is centrally about Urban Digital Twins (UDTs), their conceptualization, applications, and future realizations, with metaverse-related extensions. IC2 is not satisfied: the abstract does not explicitly propose, implement, evaluate, or formally analyze any explainability/interpretability/transparency/XAI mechanism within the digital twin; “transparency” is mentioned only as a societal risk alongside privacy/fairness, not as a DT-embedded method or evaluated approach. IC3 is not satisfied at the required explicitness: although it discusses “interaction and participation,” “participatory urban governance,” and “human-centric approaches,” it does not concretely define human roles (e.g., operator/decision-maker) nor describe a human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop architecture or evaluation. Because IC2 (and IC3) lack explicit support in the abstract, the article must be excluded under Phase 3 rules.

title: A digital twin-based biomechanical and psychosocial coupling framework for university sports dance training and evaluation
justification:
IC1 (Digital Twin central): Satisfied. The abstract frames the contribution as a “digital twin-based framework” integrating 3D modeling and real-time data for sports dance training/evaluation.

IC2 (Explicit XAI/interpretability within digital twin): Not satisfied. Although the abstract claims improved “interpretability” versus clustering baselines, it does not explicitly describe any explainability/interpretability mechanism (e.g., feature attribution, rule extraction, transparent model design, explanations to users) within the digital twin context. “Interpretability” appears as a comparative performance claim, not an explicit XAI component.

IC3 (Explicit human roles / human-in-the-loop): Not satisfied. The abstract involves students as participants being evaluated, but it does not explicitly define human roles (operator/coach/decision-maker/analyst) or describe a human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop interaction mechanism as part of the system architecture or evaluation.

Because IC2 and IC3 are missing/ambiguous based on the abstract, the article must be excluded under Phase 3 rules.

title: Predicting Recovery Factor with Digital Twins and Interpretable Machine Learning: A Case Study of South China Sea Reservoirs
justification:
IC1 (Digital Twin centrality): Satisfied. The abstract explicitly states the study uses “digital twin technology” to calculate well conversion ratios and generate “virtual development” samples to enhance recovery factor prediction, indicating DT is a defining part of the data-generation/prediction workflow.

IC2 (Explainability/XAI within DT context): Satisfied. The abstract explicitly reports “Feature importance analysis using SHAP… providing transparency,” which is a concrete interpretability mechanism applied to the model trained on the DT-augmented dataset.

IC3 (Explicit human roles / human-in-the-loop): Not satisfied. The abstract mentions “transparent… decision-making” and a “user-friendly web application… for real-time forecasting,” but it does not explicitly define any human roles (e.g., operator/engineer/analyst/decision-maker) nor describe any human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop interaction as part of the system architecture or evaluation. Usability claims alone are insufficient under the Phase 3 rule requiring explicit human-role/interaction evidence.

Because IC3 is missing, the article must be excluded.

title: Transparency in large language model (LLM)-powered digital human twins: the AI ethics perspective
justification: IC1 (Digital Twin central/defining) is not explicitly satisfied. The abstract discusses “digital human twins (DHTs)” as LLM-powered systems that mimic human behaviors, but it does not clearly define them as Digital Twins in the standard DT sense (e.g., a twin of a physical/real-world entity with a DT architecture, synchronization, or DT framework). The DT concept/architecture is therefore ambiguous based on the abstract alone. IC2 is satisfied: transparency/algorithmic opacity is a primary focus and the paper proposes concrete transparency strategies (e.g., tiered transparency models, disclosures, regulatory oversight) in the DHT context. IC3 is satisfied: it includes qualitative interviews with users and explicitly emphasizes user understanding, autonomy, and user-centric design (human-centered interaction/evaluation). Because Phase 3 requires all criteria to be explicitly and unambiguously met and IC1 is ambiguous, the article must be excluded.

title: Life prediction and health assessment of aero-engine gas path using digital twin and deep learning
justification:
IC1 (Digital Twin central): Satisfied. The abstract repeatedly frames the contribution as a health monitoring/RUL prediction system that “integrates digital twins and deep learning,” develops a “digital twin platform prototype,” and implements a closed-loop process, indicating the digital twin is a defining system concept.

IC3 (Explicit human roles / human-in-the-loop interaction): Satisfied. The abstract explicitly introduces a “multi-level virtual-reality interaction mechanism” linking physical space, health assessment, and “maintenance decision-making scenarios,” and mentions “collaborative decision-making” and “decision support,” which concretely positions humans as decision-makers interacting with the system.

IC2 (Explicit XAI/interpretability mechanism within the digital twin context): Not satisfied. Under Phase 3’s strict requirement for clear, unambiguous XAI mechanisms, this evidence is insufficient.

Because IC2 is missing/ambiguous, the article must be excluded.

title: A Framework for Standardizing the Development of Serious Games with Real-Time Self-Adaptation Capabilities Using Digital Twins
justification:

IC2 (Explicit XAI/explainability within the Digital Twin context): Not satisfied. The abstract mentions “interpretability and comprehension” only in relation to standardized data descriptions via semantic annotation/ontologies (i.e., making game elements/data portable and understandable). It does not explicitly propose, implement, or evaluate any explainability/interpretability/transparency mechanism for the digital twin’s adaptation decisions (no explanations, rationale presentation, transparency interface, traceability, or XAI methods).

IC3 (Explicit human roles / human-in-the-loop): Not satisfied. Humans are present as players providing interaction data and as domain experts defining adaptation rules and completing a usability questionnaire, but the abstract does not explicitly describe a human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop role in the digital twin’s operational decision process (e.g., oversight, intervention, interactive feedback, or human-centered control/explanation loop).

Because IC2 and IC3 are not explicitly and clearly supported in the abstract, the article must be excluded under Phase 3 rules.

title: Healthcare system optimization using digital twin

There is no explicit XAI/interpretability mechanism tied to a digital twin (or even to the decision-tree model beyond visualization), no formal explanation method, evaluation of explanations, or transparency analysis within a DT context.

IC3 (Explicit human roles/interaction): Supported. Healthcare professionals are explicitly intended users who view the GUI and use outputs for admissions/discharges/resource allocation decisions.

Because IC1 and IC2 are not clearly and explicitly satisfied based on the abstract/metadata, the article must be excluded under Phase 3 rules.

title: Implementing an AI-Based Digital Twin Analysis System for Real-Time Decision Support in a Custom-Made Sportswear SME

The abstract mentions “interpretable visual insights” and “process transparency,” but it does not explicitly propose, implement, evaluate, or formally analyze any explainability/XAI mechanism (e.g., model explanation methods, interpretable model constraints, attribution, rule extraction, counterfactuals) in the digital twin context. Final decision: Exclude because IC2 is missing/ambiguous, and Phase 3 requires all criteria to be explicitly met.

title: A cognitive digital twin for process chain anomaly detection and bottleneck analysis
justification: IC1 is satisfied: the paper’s core contribution is a proposed “cognitive digital twin (CDT)” for anomaly detection and bottleneck analysis, making Digital Twin central and defining. IC2 is satisfied: it explicitly includes “a novel explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) model” within the CDT and states it “enhances transparency and trustworthiness” and supports decision making. IC3 is not satisfied: the abstract does not explicitly define any human roles (e.g., operator/analyst/decision-maker) nor does it explicitly describe human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop or any human-centered interaction mechanism as part of the system architecture or evaluation; it only states the XAI model supports decision making without specifying humans or interaction. Per Phase 3 rules, missing IC3 requires exclusion.

title: An Immersive Digital Twin with Virtual Agent Interface for Pipeline Leak Simulation and Monitoring
justification:
IC1 (Digital Twin central): Satisfied. The abstract clearly centers on an “immersive digital twin simulation” in a “3D digital twin pipeline environment” for pipeline monitoring/training.

IC3 (Human roles / HITL interaction): Satisfied. Human roles and interaction are explicit: “operator training,” “user interaction and decision making,” and evaluation of “user trust, situational awareness, and decision making” via an “embodied conversational agent” interface.

IC2 (Explicit XAI within digital twin context): Not satisfied. Although the abstract claims integration of “explainable AI” and states “The agent can explain sensor anomalies,” it does not explicitly describe any explainability/XAI mechanism (e.g., method, model, explanation generation approach, transparency technique) implemented or evaluated within the digital twin context. The only evaluation mentioned is a planned user study about agent design factors (priming/accuracy/dominance), not an evaluation or analysis of explainability mechanisms themselves. Because IC2 is vague/high-level and lacks explicit XAI detail, the article must be excluded under Phase 3 rules.

title: Neurosymbolic Digital Twin for Cardiovascular Disease Prediction and Personalized Modeling
justification: IC1 is satisfied: the abstract explicitly frames the core contribution as “NeuroTwin is a neurosymbolic digital twin” and describes it as the unified clinical decision framework with multiple integrated modules. IC2 is satisfied: it explicitly includes an explainability mechanism within the digital twin context via the “symbolic causal discovery network (SCDN)” that yields causal structure and “converts stable edges into executable rules,” and it reports a quantified “0.942 causal explainability score.” IC3 is not satisfied: the abstract does not explicitly define any human roles (e.g., clinician/operator/analyst) and does not explicitly describe human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop interaction, oversight, or human-centered evaluation; it only states the system provides “treatment recommendations” and a “clinical decision framework,” which could be fully automated. Because IC3 is missing, the article must be excluded under Phase 3 rules.

title: Decentralized intelligence in SBs: Federated LSTM-powered digital twins for sustainability
justification:
IC1 (Digital Twin central): Satisfied. The work explicitly proposes an integrated FL–DT framework and deploys the model within a “digital twin platform” for real-time monitoring/visualization in smart buildings.

IC2 (Explicit XAI/interpretability mechanisms within DT): Not satisfied. The abstract mentions “confidence estimates,” “error diagnostics,” “system-level transparency,” and “interpretability through interactive system monitoring,” but it does not explicitly propose or evaluate an explainability/XAI method (e.g., feature attribution, interpretable model design, causal explanations, rule extraction) within the digital twin context. These statements read as monitoring/visual analytics rather than a clearly defined XAI mechanism.

IC3 (Explicit human roles or human-in/on-the-loop): Not satisfied. While it states the interface supports “timely decision-making” and “situational awareness,” the abstract does not explicitly define any human stakeholder role (operator/manager/analyst) nor describe human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop interaction as part of the architecture or evaluation.

Because IC2 and IC3 are missing/ambiguous based on the abstract, the article must be excluded under Phase 3 rules.

title: DTSafe-O: A Semantic Digital Twin Ontology for Construction Safety
justification:
IC1 (Digital Twin central): Satisfied. The abstract explicitly presents “DTSafe-O, a semantic digital twin for safety management” and describes its core components and purpose, indicating the digital twin is defining to the system.

IC2 (Explainability/XAI within DT): Satisfied. The abstract explicitly claims “computable formalization… enabling explainable and verifiable inferences” and a “validation pipeline combining reasoning, compliance checking,” plus “auditability of safety decisions,” which are clear transparency/interpretability mechanisms in the digital twin context.

IC3 (Explicit human roles or human-in/on-the-loop): NOT satisfied. The abstract discusses improved “decision processes” and “safety decisions,” but does not explicitly define any human roles (e.g., safety manager, operator, inspector) or describe human-in-the-loop / human-on-the-loop interaction as part of the system architecture or evaluation. With no concrete human-centered interaction evidence in the abstract/metadata, the paper fails IC3.

Final decision: Exclude because all three inclusion criteria must be explicitly met, and IC3 is missing.

Because all criteria must be explicitly met and IC3 is missing, the article is excluded.

title: Bayesian Networks for data contextualization in Digital Twins of complex civil infrastructures
justification:
IC1 (Digital Twin central): Satisfied. The work explicitly targets “Digital Twins (DTs) of civil infrastructures” and positions the contribution as enhancing DT capabilities.

IC2 (Explainability/XAI within DT context): Satisfied. The abstract explicitly states that “data-driven approaches lack explainability” and proposes expert-elicited Bayesian Networks to “enhance the interpretative capabilities” of DTs, i.e., an explicit interpretability mechanism in the DT setting.

IC3 (Explicit human roles / human-in-the-loop): Not satisfied. While the abstract mentions “misaligned human-machine decisions” and uses “expert-elicited” knowledge, it does not explicitly define operational human roles (e.g., operator/analyst/decision-maker) nor describe any human-in/on-the-loop interaction in the DT architecture or evaluation beyond expert knowledge elicitation during model construction. This is insufficient under Phase 3’s requirement for explicit human-role/interaction evidence.

Because IC3 is missing/weakly supported in the abstract/metadata, the article must be excluded under the Phase 3 rule that all criteria must be explicitly met.

Because IC3 is missing/insufficiently explicit, the article must be excluded under Phase 3 rules.

title: An explainable digital twin framework for skin cancer analysis using early activation meta-learner
justification:
IC1 (Digital Twin central): Partially supported but not clearly defining. The work is primarily described as a hybrid CAD system (feature extraction + meta-learning classifier). The digital twin is mentioned as an added framework to “simulate and analyze the diagnostic process… enabling real-time feedback and performance monitoring,” but the abstract does not make it the core system concept (it reads as an augmentation to the CAD pipeline rather than the central defining contribution).

IC2 (XAI within DT context): Only weakly supported. The abstract states “XAI methods were incorporated to visualize and interpret model predictions,” but it does not explicitly tie these XAI mechanisms to the digital twin (e.g., explainability of DT state/behavior, DT-driven decision support, DT-specific transparency). It could simply be standard model-level XAI for the classifier.

IC3 (Explicit human roles / HITL): Not satisfied. The abstract does not explicitly define any human roles (clinician, operator, decision-maker) and does not describe any human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop interaction mechanism or evaluation involving humans. Mentions of “clinical environments,” “real-time feedback,” and “clinical reliability” are not explicit HITL evidence.

Because IC3 is missing (and IC1/IC2 are not unambiguously satisfied as required), the article must be excluded under Phase 3 rules.

title: TailorAlert: Large Language Model-Based Personalized Alert Generation System for Road Infrastructure Management with Digital Twins

title: An Efficient and Effective Cloud Monitoring Architecture based on Data Visualization and Digital Twin Technology
justification: IC1 is satisfied: the abstract states the architecture “leverages…digital twin technology” and includes “developing an interactive digital twin for the cloud platform,” indicating Digital Twin is a central component. IC2 is not explicitly satisfied: the paper mentions “improving the interpretability of massive cloud monitoring data” via “data visualization” and a visualization mode/indicator system, but it does not explicitly propose or evaluate any explainability/XAI/transparency mechanism within the digital twin context beyond general interpretability through visualization (no explicit explanation method or XAI framing). IC3 is not explicitly satisfied: although it says the system supports “decision-making processes” and is validated via “user studies,” it does not explicitly define human roles (e.g., operator/analyst) nor describe a human-in/on-the-loop or human-centered interaction mechanism as part of the architecture/evaluation. Because IC2 and IC3 are missing/ambiguous, the article must be excluded under Phase 3 rules.

title: From Digital Twins to Digital Selves and Beyond - Perspectives for Social Modelling in a Trans-Humanist World
justification:
IC1 (Digital Twin central): Not explicitly satisfied. The abstract mentions Digital Twins as a baseline representation in cyber-physical systems, but the paper’s main contribution is framed as moving “from Digital Twins to Digital Selves” and introducing a knowledge management approach for Digital Selves; it does not clearly present a Digital Twin as the central, defining concept of a specific proposed system/architecture.
IC2 (Explainability/XAI within Digital Twin context): Not explicitly satisfied. While it calls for a “transparent and explainable knowledge base,” this is tied to Digital Selves/trans-human developments rather than an explicit XAI mechanism within a Digital Twin system (no concrete XAI method, implementation, evaluation, or formal analysis is described).
IC3 (Human roles / HITL): Not satisfied. The abstract does not define any human roles (operator/decision-maker/analyst) nor describe human-in-the-loop/on-the-loop or human-centered interaction as part of an architecture or evaluation.
Because at least IC3 is clearly missing (and IC1–IC2 are not clearly met under the strict ‘Digital Twin + XAI + human role’ requirement), the article must be excluded.
